prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map depicts an unfinished brick building corner with a window opening on the left (0.5–1.5 m away in frames 1–3), an interior room visible through the opening (2–4 m away), and a floor below covered by a coiled blue hose, loose bricks, and an inclined metal ladder or scaffold frame on the right (1–2.5 m away). Across the five frames, the camera wearer turns clockwise to the right and pitches downward while stepping onto and beginning to descend the metal ladder, bringing the ladder rails and the wearer's own torso and arms into bright near-field view (0.2–0.6 m) in frames 4–5 as the brick wall recedes to the upper left. In frame 1, a person in a blue shirt stands inside the left opening about 2.5–3 m away facing right and away from the camera wearer with a pan within their arm's reach, while a second person's lower legs appear on the right floor about 2–2.5 m away in frames 1–4 (roughly 2–3 m from the first person), both largely occluded by the brick wall and frame boundaries and looking away from the camera wearer. The depth map clearly separates the foreground ladder struts and brick wall pillar from the recessed room interior and floor clutter below—which is harder to judge in the flat RGB clutter—and shows the ladder rungs coming within arm's reach (under 0.5 m) as the wearer grasps the top rung in frame 5. However, the depth map is unreliable on the overexposed exterior ground to the far right in frame 5, rendering the distant sunlit courtyard below as completely black (infinite/missing depth) and losing the fine 3D contours of individual stacked bricks and thin hose loops.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map attempts to parse the construction scene across the five frames as the camera wearer turns right and looks down toward the ladder and brick pile, but detects only sparse fragments of the scene. In frame 1, it segments the person standing inside the left room opening (2.5–3 m away, facing right/away with head cropped at the top edge and lower body occluded by the brick wall) and labels a nearby background structure at 3–4 m as a 'chair', while in frame 5 it segments the camera wearer's own torso, arms, and hands (0.2–0.5 m away at the bottom center) as two overlapping 'person' instances grasping the ladder rung within arm's reach. Everything else is severely misclassified or omitted: individual bricks in the wall and pile (1–2 m away) are sporadically labeled as 'carrot' in frames 1–3, and nearly the entire scene in frame 2 (spanning the brick wall at 0.8 m to the floor and hose at 2 m) is covered by a single monolithic 'dining table' mask. While the masks in frames 1 and 5 help isolate the silhouette of the distant worker inside the dark doorway and the exact boundary of the wearer's reaching arms against the cluttered brick pile below, the map is highly unreliable throughout. It completely misses the metal ladder, the coiled blue hose, the brick walls in frames 3–5, and the second person's legs visible on the right floor (2–2.5 m away in frames 1–4), providing almost no usable layout information in frames 3 and 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely blank across frames 1 to 4 and detects only a single yellow body skeleton in the lower right of frame 5 corresponding to the camera wearer's own upper body and reaching arms (0.2–0.5 m from the camera). In frame 5, this skeleton maps the wearer's left and right shoulders, elbows, and wrists extending downward and forward to grasp the top rung of the metal ladder directly within arm's reach above the brick pile and coiled hose (1.5–2 m below). Because no other skeletons are rendered, the pose map fails to capture the person standing 2.5–3 m away inside the left room opening in frame 1 (who faces right, away from the camera wearer, with head cropped and legs occluded by the wall) and the second person whose lower legs and feet are visible 2–2.5 m away on the right floor across frames 1–4 (roughly 2–3 m from the first person, facing away/left). What the map adds over RGB alone is an explicit joint-level trace of the wearer's bilateral arm reach and shoulder alignment in frame 5 despite the extreme top-down egocentric foreshortening, though it fails to render magenta hand skeletons on the ladder rung. The map is unreliable wherever bodies are partially occluded or truncated by the frame edges, completely missing the wearer's emerging left hand and foot in frames 3–4 (0.4–1 m away) as well as all partially visible people in the scene.
